clue.text: Mate saw our need to change for the Victoria Line

definitions.note: a 'line' here is a remark, the famous one attributed to Queen Victoria

indicators.note: the letters of these four words are to change their order

explanation.surface: Someone tells a companion they must switch trains to get onto the London Underground's Victoria line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victoria line is a London Underground route, but here 'line' means a quotation from Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: This frosty royal remark is the saying most popularly attributed to Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Euripides' first character makes one slip

indicators.note: the words 'one slip' are made into something else, their letters reworked

explanation.surface: A tragic playwright's opening character commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a role in a play, but it is a letter: Euripides' name begins with the Greek letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek the playwright's name starts with this letter, the Greek short E.

clue.text: Always rising to welcome English official

indicators.note: the reversed word takes in a guest letter, so it surrounds it
in a down clue, rising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: always means ever

explanation.surface: Someone is forever getting up to greet an English dignitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns EVER into REVE, and E goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local magistrate or administrative officer in medieval England.

clue.text: Right name assigned to nocturnal terror

indicators.note: the letters are allotted fresh places, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Giving the correct name to a fear that strikes at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream that frightens the sleeper is exactly a terror of the night.

clue.text: Drops rents

definitions.meaning: drops of water from the eyes when crying
rents are rips or splits in fabric

explanation.definitionFit: Spelt the same, one word means teardrops and also rips, pronounced differently.

clue.text: May could (and should) have provided examples — bad move to switch around Left and Right

definitions.text: May could (and should) have provided examples

indicators.note: the letters of the pieces are switched around into a new order

explanation.surface: Reads like a political jibe: Theresa May could have set an example instead of a damaging lurch between Left and Right.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like the former Prime Minister, but 'may', 'could' and 'should' are themselves the examples. BADMOVE plus L and R are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: May, could and should are auxiliaries expressing possibility or obligation, the grammatical class of modal auxiliaries.

clue.text: Disease starts to spread — cases are being ignored, everyone's scared

indicators.note: the opening letters of the seven words that follow are taken

parts.words: spread — cases are being ignored, everyone's scared

explanation.surface: A disease begins to spread while cases are overlooked and everyone panics.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabies is a contagious skin infestation caused by mites, a recognised medical complaint.

clue.text: At sea, it's dead wrong going round east

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round, enclosing, the other piece
the words are put wrong, scrambling their letters

parts.note: the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: A sailor at sea gets it fatally wrong by steering round to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' feels like part of a sailor's scene but is the definition: bewildered. 'east' gives the Orient, and 'going round' means the jumbled letters enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea in the idiomatic sense means being confused and lost, without bearings.

clue.text: When admitted into court, start to exude class

indicators.note: a piece is let inside the other, as into a building

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Once you are admitted into court, you begin to radiate class.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, as in the Hindu system.

clue.text: Unable to sleep, pimp might be involved in this

definitions.text: Unable to sleep, pimp might be involved in this

parts.words: Unable to sleep, pimp might be involved in this
parts.note: the insomniac's traditional remedy; in old shepherds' tallies (yan, tan, tethera, methera, pimp) 'pimp' is the word for five

explanation.surface: Seems to hint at a sleazy night-time activity linked to a pimp.
explanation.walkthrough: Pimp is not a procurer: in the traditional northern English sheep-counting rhyme it is the number five.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomniacs are told to tally imaginary flock animals jumping a fence to drift off.

clue.text: In Asia, drug distributed after I left by those in charge

indicators.note: the letters are distributed into a new order
a letter is left out of the jumble, removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A drug is handed out in Asia once the speaker has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges INASIADRUG, and 'after I left' takes out one I.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardians are people with responsibility for others, such as keepers or custodians.

clue.text: Its glue dissolved, becoming most hideous

indicators.note: the words are dissolved and their letters reformed

explanation.surface: An object's glue has melted away, leaving it in an ugly state.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideous means very unpleasant to look at, so the superlative is the least attractive.

clue.text: What might be volatile row becomes even more piquant

parts.note: sal volatile is smelling salts, so sal is what might take the word volatile
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A volatile quarrel grows even spicier.
explanation.walkthrough: SAL is Latin for salt, as in sal volatile, the smelling salts.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquant food has a sharp tang; a saltier dish has still more bite.

clue.text: Dance beat with scat

parts.note: to tan is to beat, as in tanning someone's hide
scat means go away

explanation.surface: A dance performed to a rhythm with scat singing.
explanation.walkthrough: Scat looks like jazz singing; here it is the order to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Turn into beast, being stubborn

indicators.note: the letters turn into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone turns into a beast by refusing to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate is a near-synonym of stubborn, describing someone unyielding.

clue.text: Supplement extremely rare supplies; exclude the one dispatches were meant for

definitions.text: the one dispatches were meant for

parts.note: to supplement is to add

indicators.note: the extreme, outermost letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to top up scarce supplies while leaving someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' reaches past the semicolon: RE, SS and EE are the ends of rare, supplies and exclude.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatches are letters or messages, and the person they are sent to is their recipient.

clue.text: Striking diet, using bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: An eye-catching diet that relies on bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is the slang for crazy, not fruit in the diet.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword describes someone distinguished and impressive in bearing.

clue.text: When unable to move screens outside you've got these resources available

indicators.note: one piece stands outside the other, around it

parts.note: nets are screens, as on windows
as can mean when
set means fixed, unable to move

explanation.surface: Stuck behind screens, you still have these to call on.
explanation.definitionFit: Net assets are what a business holds after liabilities, the resources it truly has.

clue.text: Across-the-board hugs providing revenue for the government

indicators.note: the outer word hugs, embraces, the inner letters

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging
X is a cross, the shape of things lying across each other
the article becomes A, swapping definite for indefinite

explanation.surface: A sweeping, across-the-board embrace that brings in money for the state.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphens disguise three separate pieces: Across, the and board.
explanation.definitionFit: Income that can be levied yields money for the Treasury, so it is liable to duty.

clue.text: BT tower's hidden within foliage

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: taken as written
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a tower of broken-down cars; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: The BT Tower in London is screened by leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The BT Tower is a London telecom landmark; here 'tower' is the breakdown service that tows cars, the RAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A bract is a modified leaf at the base of a flower, so a piece of the leafage.

clue.text: Inanimate cat I transported about — story of my life!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about the other piece
the letters are carried into a new order

parts.note: a bio is a short life story

explanation.surface: A weary sigh about lugging the cat around: story of my life!
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' makes ATIC from CATI, placed about BIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Abiotic means non-living, not derived from living organisms.

clue.text: Exchanging dodgy messages with former partner in crime

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a sting is a swindle, a confidence crime
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Swapping shady texts with an ex who was an accomplice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers sending sexually explicit messages by phone, the dodgy kind.

clue.text: What's ground for girls to be unhappy, dropping Latin at beginning of term

indicators.note: the word is made unhappy, its letters disturbed
a letter is dropped, removed
only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Grounds for schoolgirls to be miserable: Latin dropped as the term starts.
explanation.walkthrough: GIRLS rearranged without L gives GRIS, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: Grist is corn brought to the mill for grinding.

clue.text: Admission I dislike old fogeys like Pound and Lowell

parts.note: an admission of what I am is I'M
agist, a variant spelling of ageist, means prejudiced against the old

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to disliking old fuddy-duddies.
explanation.walkthrough: Ezra Pound and Amy Lowell are poets, not money and a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Both poets belonged to the early twentieth-century movement favouring clear, precise images.

clue.text: Distant admiration initially when trick is turned on its head

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used
in a down clue, standing on its head means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: to fool is to trick

explanation.surface: Admiration fades into coolness when a trick backfires.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means cool and reserved, keeping one's distance from others.

clue.text: Displaying affection wildly can be grim

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: Warns that unrestrained behaviour can turn grim.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugging someone is a physical way of showing fondness.

clue.text: Exposed old vehicle to Australian desert initiation

parts.note: a ute, utility vehicle, is an Australian pick-up truck

indicators.note: the initiation, beginning, of the word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: An old Aussie vehicle exposed during a desert ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outed is to have a secret, often sexuality, revealed publicly.

clue.text: Ideal gift given before he's apologised or she's reconsidered, say

definitions.text: he's apologised or she's reconsidered, say

indicators.note: the second word's piece is given before the first

parts.note: a present is a gift
perfect means ideal

explanation.surface: An ideal present offered before apologies and second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given before' reverses the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb forms 'has apologised' and 'has reconsidered' are the tense built with have plus a past participle.
